selloff.title: Early-November selloff
selloff.text: Memory names fell 19 to 26% between the 29 Oct close and 6 Nov while contract prices were still rising. Reported drivers: post-midterm rotation out of AI infrastructure after data-centre ballot measures passed restricting new builds, worries about export-approval delays for Korean HBM shipments, and profit-taking after a 5x to 10x year. The table below computes each name's live distance from its 52-week high.

bull.t: Custom silicon is compounding, not optional
bull.d: Custom XPU revenue went from about US$1.5bn in FY26 to a target above US$12bn in FY29 and about US$30bn by FY31, with silicon shipping to all four US hyperscalers and more than 35 sockets at the top four. Hyperscalers want a credible second source to Broadcom, and Marvell is the only scaled one.

bull.t: Guidance keeps rising while the stock fell
bull.d: FY28 revenue is guided to about US$20bn (+67%) with data centre about US$18bn, pulled forward a year. Q3 FY27 revenue of about US$3.15bn was reconfirmed on 2 Nov with a narrower range. The share price roughly halved in a month on deal and macro worries, not on operating news.

bull.t: Optics is the next bottleneck and Marvell is buying the laser
bull.d: Scale-up and scale-across fabrics are moving from copper to optics. Marvell already leads 800G and 1.6T PAM4 DSPs and coherent pluggables (US$0.5bn going to more than US$1bn by FY28). Lumentum adds indium-phosphide lasers, transceivers and optical circuit switching, with more than US$1bn of run-rate synergies and year-one EPS accretion.

Strategic agreements with AWS, Nvidia (custom XPUs plus NVLink Fusion scale-up networking, Mar 2026) and Google (a stated US$120bn opportunity over 6.5 years). Management says no single socket will dominate by FY31, which answers the Trainium concentration worry.

bull.t: The market is pricing the dilution, not the earnings power
bull.d: Lumentum holders get about 33% of the combined company at a fixed 4.5 ratio. Because MRVL fell after announcement, the implied price is now below LITE's unaffected level, so Marvell is paying less in value terms than the headline US$115bn. Rosenblatt kept a Buy with a US$300 target; most covering analysts still rate the stock a Buy.

Micron, SK hynix and Samsung just printed record quarters with HBM supply sold out into 2027. Every HBM stack and every XPU needs more SerDes, more switching and more optics per dollar of compute, which is Marvell's content story.

bear.d: A fixed 4.5 ratio hands Lumentum holders 33% of the company and the close is not until 1H CY2028. TD Cowen cut to Hold with a US$175 target, arguing the deal lands near an optical demand peak and the two firms did not need to merge to collaborate.

bear.t: Custom silicon is a knife fight on margin
bear.d: Broadcom holds roughly 60 to 70% of custom AI ASICs. MediaTek has won multi-generation programs, and Alchip and GUC are pressuring XPU design margins. Marvell's share is estimated around 15%, and programs are lumpy and few.
Data centre is 79% of revenue and a handful of hyperscalers drive it. Shipments billed to China were 42% of Q2 FY27 revenue by destination, and one distributor was more than a third of sales.

Data-centre ballot measures passed on 3 Nov restricting new builds in several jurisdictions, and AI infrastructure names sold off hard the next two sessions. Any slowdown in hyperscaler capex hits Marvell's FY28 to FY31 targets directly.

watch.d: Expected early December 2026 (last year's Q3 was 2 Dec; date not yet confirmed). Revenue is pre-announced at about US$3.15bn; the tell is custom revenue acceleration into 2H and the Q4 guide against the US$3bn+ exit run-rate.
The deal monitor above compares 4.5x MRVL with LITE's price live. A widening discount signals doubt about the vote or the ratio.

watch.t: Broadcom FQ4 (Dec) and hyperscaler capex guides (late Jan)
watch.d: Read-through for custom ASIC share and 2027 optics volumes.
Micron FQ1 FY27 in late December; TrendForce 1Q27 contract-price outlook in December. DRAM tightness supports the HBM-to-XPU content thesis; a NAND rollover is the first cycle crack to watch.

competitor_notes.CRDO: Active electrical cables and optical DSPs; the copper alternative to Marvell's optics

competitor_notes.AMD: Merchant GPU challenger; benchmark for custom-vs-merchant share debate
competitor_notes.MTK: Rising custom ASIC challenger; reported multi-generation hyperscaler wins
competitor_notes.ALCHIP: Taiwan ASIC design service; price competition on XPU programs
competitor_notes.GUC: TSMC-affiliated ASIC design service; same pressure point as Alchip
competitor_notes.LITE: Merger target; lasers, transceivers and optical circuit switching
